prompt:
Build a decentralized closed-loop collision-avoidance simulation for exactly eight car-like vehicles. Read multiagent_mission from the MATLAB base workspace. It is a scalar struct with these public fields: duration_s, a real scalar from 8 to 15 s; initial_positions_m, a real 8-by-2 [x,y] matrix in metres with coordinates from -20 to 20 m and non-overlapping initial discs; goal_positions_m, a real 8-by-2 [x,y] matrix in metres with coordinates from -20 to 20 m; initial_speeds_mps, a real 8-by-1 vector from 0.5 to 3.0 m/s; initial_headings_rad, a real 8-by-1 vector from -pi to pi rad; agent_radius_m, a real scalar from 0.7 to 1.2 m; preferred_speed_mps, a real scalar from 1.0 to 3.0 m/s; maximum_acceleration_mps2, a real scalar from 1.0 to 4.0 m/s^2; maximum_steering_tangent, a real scalar from 0.8 to 2.5; and passive_agents, a logical 8-by-1 vector whose true entries identify passive vehicles. Each active vehicle must navigate toward its own goal using its measured position, speed, and heading while treating all seven other moving vehicles as obstacles. Combine goal-seeking control with online safety filtering based on relative position and velocity, finite vehicle radius, and collision-cone or velocity-obstacle reasoning. Apply bounded steering-tangent and longitudinal-acceleration commands to integrated car-like dynamics. Passive vehicles must retain their initial velocity, accept zero control, and remain visible to every active safety filter. For both initial_headings_rad and every logged heading_rad, zero points along the positive x-axis and positive angles rotate toward the positive y-axis; the corresponding planar velocity is [speed*cos(heading), speed*sin(heading)].

Every published mission field must affect the corresponding initial state, goal, geometry, control bound, preferred motion, passive role, or duration. Collision avoidance must arise from mutually coupled state observations and changed control actions rather than pre-scripted nonintersecting paths. The same controller must handle symmetric crossings, offset starts, unequal approach speeds, and a moving passive obstacle. Vehicle centres must remain separated by their combined radii, solver failures must be exposed, and active vehicles must make causal progress toward their goals.

Log two complete-run Timeseries named agent_state and agent_control. agent_state has exactly 40 channels in this order: [agent1_x_m, agent1_y_m, agent1_speed_mps, agent1_heading_rad, agent1_goal_reached, agent2_x_m, agent2_y_m, agent2_speed_mps, agent2_heading_rad, agent2_goal_reached, agent3_x_m, agent3_y_m, agent3_speed_mps, agent3_heading_rad, agent3_goal_reached, agent4_x_m, agent4_y_m, agent4_speed_mps, agent4_heading_rad, agent4_goal_reached, agent5_x_m, agent5_y_m, agent5_speed_mps, agent5_heading_rad, agent5_goal_reached, agent6_x_m, agent6_y_m, agent6_speed_mps, agent6_heading_rad, agent6_goal_reached, agent7_x_m, agent7_y_m, agent7_speed_mps, agent7_heading_rad, agent7_goal_reached, agent8_x_m, agent8_y_m, agent8_speed_mps, agent8_heading_rad, agent8_goal_reached], with the per-agent unit pattern [m, m, m/s, rad, 1]. agent_control has exactly 32 channels in this order: [agent1_steering_tangent, agent1_acceleration_mps2, agent1_solver_cost, agent1_solver_exit_flag, agent2_steering_tangent, agent2_acceleration_mps2, agent2_solver_cost, agent2_solver_exit_flag, agent3_steering_tangent, agent3_acceleration_mps2, agent3_solver_cost, agent3_solver_exit_flag, agent4_steering_tangent, agent4_acceleration_mps2, agent4_solver_cost, agent4_solver_exit_flag, agent5_steering_tangent, agent5_acceleration_mps2, agent5_solver_cost, agent5_solver_exit_flag, agent6_steering_tangent, agent6_acceleration_mps2, agent6_solver_cost, agent6_solver_exit_flag, agent7_steering_tangent, agent7_acceleration_mps2, agent7_solver_cost, agent7_solver_exit_flag, agent8_steering_tangent, agent8_acceleration_mps2, agent8_solver_cost, agent8_solver_exit_flag], with the per-agent unit pattern [1, m/s^2, 1, 1]. Both logs must begin at 0 s, remain finite, and reach multiagent_mission.duration_s. State channels must come from the integrated vehicle dynamics and control channels must be the commands actually applied to those dynamics. Hard-coded private paths, replayed outputs, copied goal positions presented as vehicle state, fabricated logs, independent uncoupled agents, or safety signals disconnected from applied steering and acceleration are not acceptable. Save the completed model as cand_XAUTO12.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAUTO12.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
